what_its_for: Apalutamide is used to treat prostate cancer. It works by blocking the effects of testosterone (a male hormone) that can help prostate cancer cells grow. It is used for prostate cancer that has not spread to other parts of the body (non-metastatic) or for prostate cancer that has spread but still responds to hormone therapy (metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer).
how_to_take: Take apalutamide by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablets. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. You will usually take 4 tablets together as one daily dose.
dosing: The usual dose is 240 mg (four 60 mg tablets) taken once daily by mouth. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on side effects or other medications you take.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and remember the same day, take it as soon as you remember. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store apalutamide tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and store it in a dry place, away from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medications down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medication, as it can affect how the drug works in your body. Apalutamide can interact with many other medications, so tell ALL your doctors and pharmacists every medicine you take, including vitamins, supplements, and herbal products. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should NEVER handle crushed or broken apalutamide tablets. Men taking this drug should use effective birth control (condoms) during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose if their partner could become pregnant. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have seizures.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: seizures or convulsions, sudden falls, skin rash (which can be severe and widespread), chest pain or shortness of breath, signs of a stroke such as sudden numbness, weakness, confusion, trouble speaking, or vision changes, severe dizziness or fainting, broken bones or fractures, or signs of heart problems. Also call your doctor if you feel unusually tired, have mood changes, or notice any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Apalutamide works continuously while you are taking it. It may take several weeks to months before your doctor can measure its full effect through blood tests (PSA levels) and scans. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): No dose adjustment is typically needed, but older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like falls and fractures, so use extra caution. Kidney or liver problems: Mild to moderate kidney or liver problems usually do not require a dose change, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Severe liver disease may require special consideration. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This drug is NOT for use in women, and women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should never handle crushed or broken tablets. Men: If your partner is pregnant or could become pregnant, use condoms during treatment and for 3 months after stopping. Children: This medication is not approved for use in children.
